name: Sweet potato vine

schedule.notes: Buy plants or root your own cuttings in water. Wait for warm soil — cold-shocked plants stall for weeks.
Pinch tips to keep mounding habit dense and take cuttings any time. Frost blackens the foliage overnight — pull and compost, or root cuttings in water indoors to overwinter.

harvest.cues: Grown for foliage, not fruit. Pinch growing tips when stems are 8+ in to encourage branching.
harvest.storageNotes: Root 4 in stem cuttings in a jar of water on a sunny windowsill — they hold all winter and pot up cheap next spring. Tubers can be lifted and stored frost-free but are tough and bland (not bred for eating).

varieties.name: Sweet Caroline Raven
varieties.notes: Near-black arrowhead leaves on a compact mounding habit. Sun-tolerant and less rampant than older 'Blackie' types. PP31,837.

varieties.name: Blackie
varieties.notes: The original dark cultivar — deep purple-black, maple-shaped lobed leaves, vigorous trailing to 6 ft.

varieties.name: Marguerite
varieties.notes: Bright chartreuse heart-shaped leaves. The lime-green counterpart used to brighten dark pairings.

notes: Grown for foliage, not tubers — ornamental cultivars produce poor, woody, sometimes inedible roots despite being the same species as edible sweet potato. Trailing or mounding by cultivar; thrives in heat that flattens other annuals. Cheap to propagate: snip a stem, stick it in water for a week, plant it. Patented varieties (PP numbers) restrict commercial propagation but personal cuttings are fine.
